blocks.text: Why Finder work eats more of a support day than it should

Support work leaves files everywhere. An export lands in Downloads. A log sits in a folder named after a ticket. Screenshots pile up on the desktop. Each file costs a few seconds to find, and those seconds add up across a shift. Finder is where most of that searching happens, so small habits matter more than they seem.

HDI's SupportWorld article gives a first-call resolution target of 70% to 80% for a good service center. The article is undated, so treat the number as a rough benchmark. Time spent hunting for a file comes out of the same window you need to close the ticket.
Set up Finder views for fast triage

Finder has four views, and you switch between them with toolbar buttons. Apple's guide names Icon, List, Column and Gallery. Pick the view for the job in front of you, not the one you used last time. A view that suits a photo folder is often the wrong one for a log sweep.

rows: A quick visual scan of a folder
Thumbnails help you spot an image or screenshot fast
Sorting by name, date or size
Rows stay readable when a folder is long
You see each level, so you never lose your place
Each selected file shows a large preview
blocks.caption: Switch views from the toolbar, per Apple's Organize your files guide.

blocks.text: Sorting by name can bury the folder you need. Turn on Keep Folders on Top. Go to View > Show View Options, then choose Keep Folders on Top. Folders stay above files when you sort by name, which puts the subfolder you want first.

The Group button in the toolbar sorts items into groups. Use it when one folder mixes logs, configuration files and screenshots. The odd file out stands apart once the groups appear. Group first, then look at the odd file.

blocks.title: Check column settings after an update
blocks.text: MacRumors reports that macOS 27 adds autosize and reset controls for Finder columns. If a column looks cramped after you update, look for those controls before you resize by hand. Ask Lazur where they are.
Find files with Spotlight and Quick Look

Spotlight is the quickest way to reach a file you can name but cannot place. Press ⌘ Space, type part of the name, and open the result. Apple's Spotlight page says you can hold Command to locate a file in Finder instead of opening it.

items: Type part of the file name, such as the ticket number.
Hold ⌘ to locate the result in Finder instead of opening it.
Select the file in Finder and press Space to preview it with Quick Look.

blocks.text: Quick Look is the habit that saves the most time during triage. Select a file in Finder and press Space. Use it on logs, PDFs and screenshots before you open anything heavy. You decide what to open after you see what is inside.
When a file does not show up

Apple's pages do not describe Finder search scope, indexing or privacy exclusions. A missing result does not prove the file is gone. Open the folder directly in Column view and look there first. That check takes less time than a second search, and it shows you what the search missed.
Tag files so the next person can find them

Tags are colored labels you attach to files and folders. Apple's tagging page says Control-1 through Control-7 add or remove favorite tags, and Control-0 removes all tags. You manage the tag list in Finder > Settings > Tags.

rows: Add or remove a favorite tag
Each number maps to one favorite tag
Clears every tag on the selected item
Set up the tags your team uses
blocks.caption: Tag shortcuts from Apple's Tag files and folders page.

blocks.text: The Control-click menu shows up to seven tags, according to Apple. Apple does not state a maximum number of tags per item. Keep your list short, so the menu stays useful during a busy queue.

A common mistake is making a new tag name for every ticket. The result is a long list of near-duplicate tags and no clean way to group them. Pick two or three tags for states such as waiting, done and escalated, and stick to them.

blocks.title: Tahoe moved the Tags menu
blocks.text: A MacPowerUsers forum post says that in macOS Tahoe, Tags appears in the File menu only when files are selected. With a folder selected, that slot offers Customize Folder instead. This is a user report, not an Apple statement, so check it on your own Mac.
Build Smart Folders for recurring ticket work

A Smart Folder is a saved search that updates itself. Apple's guide says to choose File > New Smart Folder, use the + button to set criteria, and save the folder to the sidebar. Apple's pages describe no Finder templates, so a Smart Folder is the closest thing to a reusable view.

A regular folder still has its place. Create one with File > New Folder or Shift-⌘N. Use a normal folder for files you own and store. Use a Smart Folder when the files are spread across several folders and you want one view of them.
Worked example: one folder for one ticket

items: Open the ticket's export folder in Column view.
Select the files that matter, then press Space to preview each one.
Tag the keepers with Control-1, your ticket tag.
Create a Smart Folder for that tag with File > New Smart Folder, then save it to the sidebar.
Hold fn and dictate the handoff note, then paste it into the ticket.

blocks.text: Now the sidebar shows one folder that lists every file tagged for the ticket. Other tickets stay out of the way. Remove the Smart Folder when the ticket closes, and the tags stay on the files as a record.
Ask Lazur where a Finder control is

Hold ⌥⌘ and ask your question out loud. Lazur sees your screen while you hold the keys, and it answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time.

items: Hold ⌥⌘ and ask, for example, where the Group button is.
Lazur answers out loud and circles the control on screen.
For a how-to question, Lazur gives one step and waits.
You click. Lazur moves to the next step only after you do.

blocks.text: Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. Think of it as a sharp friend who points at the screen, not a pair of hands. That limit keeps you in charge of every change to a customer's files.
Dictate notes and drafts while you work

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Dictation is included, and it is handy for ticket notes even when you are not in Finder.

Dictate the handoff note while the Finder window is still open. Name the folder, the view and the file, then read the text back before you paste it. Voice input can mishear rare product names and ticket codes, so check those first.
Privacy, memory and what stays on the Mac

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps memory of what you asked and did on the Mac.
Check your company's policy before you let any tool see customer files. A screenshot of a ticket can show names, addresses or account details. Close sensitive windows before you hold the shortcut.
What Lazur does not do in Finder
Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available yet.

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. For browser work, read the [Chrome guide for IT support technicians](/for/it-support-technicians/chrome). For chat, read the [Slack guide](/for/it-support-technicians/slack).
Edge cases to plan for in Finder

A file can sit in the right folder and still look wrong. Check the view first. Then check the sort order. Then check whether a Smart Folder is showing a saved search instead of the folder itself. Most confusion comes from one of those three.
Gallery view can feel slow in a folder of large images or big documents, because each selected file shows a large preview. Switch to List view for a bulk sort, then switch back for review.
Several Finder windows create their own clutter. Keep one window per ticket and close the rest. Column view in a single window usually works better than four windows open at once.
Mistakes that slow Finder work down on a Mac

items: Using Icon view for a folder of logs. List view is easier to scan by name and date.
Assuming Spotlight searches every folder. Apple does not describe Finder search scope.
Making a new tag name for every ticket. Keep a short, fixed tag set.
Looking for Tags in the File menu with a folder selected on Tahoe.
Expecting Lazur to click through a dialog. It guides you, and you click.
Trusting an old menu path after an update. Menus can move between macOS versions.

blocks.text: Which macOS version this guide covers

This guide covers macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple's Mac User Guide names it in the version selector. MacRumors reports that Golden Gate came out in mid-September 2026. It also says macOS Golden Gate 27.2 was the first major update, and 27.3 is in public beta.

If your Mac runs an older release, menu paths and view options may differ. Check the version before you follow a menu path step by step. A path that fails on your screen is often a version difference, not a mistake.
Next steps for your Finder routine

Start with Column view and Space for Quick Look. Next, tag one ticket with Control-1 through Control-7 and build one Smart Folder for that tag. Then ask Lazur where any control is that you cannot find. You can [download Lazur](/download) for Mac, and the trial needs no credit card.

faq.question: Is there a special Finder for IT support technicians on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Finder is the built-in file browser on every Mac, and Apple's guide describes no Finder templates. The closest tools are Smart Folders and saved tag sets, and the steps above show how to set them up.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Finder for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at controls, explains them, guides you one step at a time and drafts text. It waits for each click, and you do the clicking.

faq.question: Which macOS version do these steps cover?
faq.answer: macOS 27 Golden Gate, according to Apple's Mac User Guide. MacRumors reports the release in mid-September 2026, with 27.2 as the first major update. Menus can move between releases, so check your version first.

faq.question: Why does my tag not appear in the Control-click menu?
faq.answer: Apple says the Control-click shortcut menu shows up to seven tags. Apple does not state a maximum number of tags per item. If a tag is missing from the menu, trim the list or use Control-1 through Control-7 for the tags you use most.

faq.question: Where is Tags in the File menu on macOS Tahoe?
faq.answer: A MacPowerUsers forum post says Tags appears in the File menu only when files are selected. With a folder selected, that slot shows Customize Folder instead. That is a user report, not an Apple statement. Select a file to see the Tags item.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my screen all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored.

faq.question: Can Lazur search my files for me?
faq.answer: Lazur answers questions about what is on screen, and it handles everyday actions such as timers, Reminders, Calendar events, notes and web search. For file search, use Spotlight. Apple's Spotlight page describes ⌘ Space and holding Command to locate a result in Finder.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.
